description:
We are a team of Computer Science Engineering (Data Science) students from JNNCE, Shivamogga, and we are excited to take on the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.  

We are interested in the storytelling challenge about the hardware NASA has left on the Moon, Mars and in deep space. We want to turn it into an interactive experience that helps school students learn about these missions.

Our skills: web development (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), data handling, and design.
summary:
Forgotten in Space: Every Mission Leaves a Story is an interactive 3D web platform that transforms humanity’s dormant spacecraft and robotic explorers across the Solar System, Moon, Mars, and Deep Space into living cultural monuments. Developed using Three.js, Streamlit, and Google Gemini AI, the application combines interactive 3D planetary exploration, authentic 3D spacecraft simulators (Opportunity, Viking 1, Ingenuity), historical audio narratives, and live NASA Open Data photography.

The project directly addresses the Off-World Artifacts challenge by reframing inactive hardware—from Apollo lunar modules to Martian rovers—from "forgotten debris" into celebrated monuments of human ingenuity. Users can inspect exact landing coordinates, analyze verified telemetry, and converse directly with the spacecraft via grounded first-person AI personas.

This project is vital because it preserves humanity’s extraterrestrial heritage as we enter the Artemis era. Offering 100% free, zero-login access for students (ages 12–18), it demystifies complex aerospace engineering and inspires the next generation of STEM leaders.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

"Forgotten in Space: Every Mission Leaves a Story" is an interactive 3D web platform that transforms humanity's resting off-world spacecraft and planetary explorers across the Solar System, Moon, Mars, and Deep Space into living cultural monuments.

The application operates through four interconnected technological systems:

  • Interactive 3D WebGL Simulation: Powered by Three.js, users navigate a real-time 3D Solar System with Keplerian orbital paths, visit the Martian and Lunar surfaces with 360-degree interactive camera controls, and warp into Deep Space via seamless cinematic descent videos. Users can inspect authentic, detailed 3D models of iconic craft—Opportunity, Viking 1, and Ingenuity—with custom orbit and lighting controls.
  • Dynamic NASA Open Data Integration: The application queries official NASA APIs (images-api.nasa.gov and NASA APOD) in real time to present high-resolution surface photography, scientific observations, and instrument telemetry.
  • Cloud Telemetry via Supabase: A relational PostgreSQL database provides verified landing coordinates, mission lifespans, odometry, power sources, and formal commemorations for every featured mission.
  • First-Person Gemini AI Chatbot & Spatial Audio: Users can listen to authentic narrated audio stories and converse directly with spacecraft through a Google Gemini AI persona engine that roleplays in the first person as the machine itself, grounded in verified mission records.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Hands-on, Experiential STEM Learning: Replaces static textbook paragraphs with interactive 3D physics, tactile planetary navigation, and first-person engagement, making complex aerospace engineering concepts intuitive.
  • Accurate Scientific Truth (Zero Hallucination): Ensures students learn verified historical facts by grounding all AI responses in official NASA mission logs and Supabase telemetry rather than unverified generative text.
  • Dual-Level Pedagogical Flexibility: Includes an audience selector (Junior Explorer for ages 12–14 vs. Senior Enthusiast for ages 15–18) that adapts explanations between visual analogies and rigorous physics/spectrometry.
  • Universal Accessibility: 100% free with zero paywalls, zero login screens, and zero software downloads—accessible to anyone with an internet browser on any computer, tablet, or classroom device.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Preserving Human Space Exploration Heritage: As NASA's Artemis program and future Mars expeditions prepare to launch, our platform establishes a digital catalog and awareness of historic landing sites as sacred archaeological monuments.
  • Inspiring the Next Generation of Scientists & Engineers: Sparks curiosity and emotional connection with space exploration for young students, encouraging them to pursue careers in robotics, astrophysics, aerospace engineering, and planetary science.
  • Honoring the People Behind the Missions: Celebrates the thousands of engineers, scientists, and flight controllers whose dedication enabled these groundbreaking voyages.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Languages: Python 3.11+ (backend orchestration, data pipelines) and JavaScript ES6+ (frontend logic, WebGL loops, UI interactivity).
  • Application Framework: Streamlit (web server, dynamic session routing, component iframe integration).
  • 3D Graphics & Rendering: Three.js (r128), HTML5 WebGL, OrbitControls, and Google DRACO 3D geometry compression/decompression algorithms.
  • Artificial Intelligence: Google Gemini AI API (Gemini 1.5 Flash / Pro models with structured persona system instructions and RAG grounding).
  • Database & Cloud Backend: Supabase Cloud PostgreSQL (relational telemetry storage).
  • NASA Open Data APIs: NASA Image and Video Library REST API (images-api.nasa.gov), NASA APOD API.
  • Cloud Hosting & Deployment: GitHub, Streamlit Community Cloud, and Render Linux container hosting.

5. How is your project creative?

  • First-Person Conversational Machine Persona: Rather than an impersonal search assistant, the AI embodies the physical machine itself ("I am the Opportunity rover. My wheels arrived at Meridiani Planum in 2004..."), creating an empathetic bond between students and historical artifacts.
  • Cinematic Planetary Warp Sequences: Features seamless edge-to-edge video transitions simulating atmospheric entry and interplanetary travel between the Solar System, Moon, Mars, and Deep Space.
  • Resilient Hybrid Media Studio: Instead of repeating duplicate 3D models for rovers without existing 3D scans, the system intelligently adapts: craft with authentic 3D models load interactive WebGL simulators; unmodeled craft automatically open a high-resolution NASA Mission Photography & Media Studio with authentic archival imagery and telemetry.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Performance on Low-End Devices: Utilized DRACO 3D model compression and optimized Three.js render loops to guarantee fluid frame rates on standard classroom laptops, tablets, and mobile devices without requiring dedicated GPUs.
  • Scientific Rigor vs. Creative Accessibility: Balanced rigorous historical and geological accuracy with an engaging, cinematic, gamified aesthetic that keeps younger students excited without compromising educational integrity.
  • Zero-Friction Access: Strictly avoided login barriers, passwords, or permissions to ensure immediate, barrier-free access for hackathon judges and global classrooms alike.
  • Network & Host Resilience: Engineered multi-tiered asset fallback pipelines (local server endpoints paired with CORS-enabled GitHub Raw CDN mirrors) to ensure 100% uptime for all 3D models, textures, audio stories, and video transitions.
